questions.prompt: The Crusades were wars fought mainly over control of…
questions.why: Religious wars between European Christians and Muslim powers over Jerusalem and the Holy Land. Friday's gap — now it's yours.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Romeo and Juliet is set in which Italian city?
questions.why: Fair Verona, where we lay our scene. (Mantua is the trap — it's where Romeo gets banished TO.)

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In feudalism, knights received land from their lord in return for…
questions.why: Land down, service up — the whole pyramid runs on that exchange. You taught this chain back to me last week.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Globalisation means the world's countries becoming more…
questions.why: Trade, travel, tech, culture — the connections thicken. That's globalisation in one word.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: After the Western Roman Empire fell in 476 CE, Europe entered the…
questions.why: Rome falls → the medieval (Middle Ages) period begins. It's the doorway your whole Term 3 unit walks through.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A fish tank is 40 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm tall. What volume of water fills it to the brim?
questions.why: 40 × 25 × 30 = 30,000 cm³. Multiply all three dimensions — 95 is what you get if you ADD them, and adding is the classic slip.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: An experiment tests whether the AMOUNT OF FERTILISER changes tomato yield. Which is the independent variable?
questions.why: Independent = the thing YOU change on purpose (fertiliser). Dependent = what you measure (yield). Controlled = kept the same (water, plant count). Wednesday's miss — locked in now.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which moment BEST shows the play's big idea of love overpowering inherited hate?
options: Juliet marrying Romeo despite the family feud
Tybalt duelling Mercutio in the street
questions.answer: Juliet marrying Romeo despite the family feud
questions.why: The marriage is love directly overriding the hate she was BORN into — the exact theme you nailed in Friday's teach-back. The duel is the hate side of the scales.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Why did the medieval Church hold so much power — even over kings?
options: It controlled salvation, and even kings feared excommunication
It owned every farm in Europe
Kings were required to train as priests
questions.answer: It controlled salvation, and even kings feared excommunication
questions.why: In a world where everyone believed in heaven and hell, the Church held the keys — cutting a king off from salvation could break his rule without a single sword.
